verses.1:1: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.1:2: Grace be to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: We ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren, as is fitting, because your faith increases abundantly, and the love of every one of you all abounds toward one another,
verses.1:4: so that we ourselves glory in you among the churches of God for your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions which you endure.
verses.1:5: This is plain proof of the righteous judgment of God, that you may be accounted worthy of the kingdom of God, for the sake of which you also suffer;
verses.1:6: since indeed it is righteous with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
verses.1:7: and to you who are afflicted, rest with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of His power
verses.1:8: in a flame of fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
verses.1:9: These shall pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His might,
verses.1:10: when He comes to be glorified in His saints and to be marveled at among all who have believed—for our testimony to you was believed—in that day.
verses.1:11: To this end we also pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of His calling, and bring to fulfillment every desire for goodness and work of faith with power,
verses.1:12: so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2:1: Now we urge you, brethren, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to Him,
verses.2:2: that you not be quickly shaken from your mind or alarmed, whether by spirit or by word or by letter as if from us, to the effect that the day of the Lord has already come.
verses.2:3: Let no one deceive you in any manner; for that day shall not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of perdition,
verses.2:4: who opposes and exalts himself above everything called a god or an object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God, displaying himself to be God.
verses.2:5: Do you not remember that while I was still with you, I used to tell you these things?
verses.2:6: And now you know what restrains him, so that he may be revealed in his own season.
verses.2:7: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains for the present remains until he is taken out of the way.
verses.2:8: And then the lawless one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall slay with the breath of His mouth and destroy by the appearing of His coming.
verses.2:9: The coming of that lawless one is in accordance with the working of Satan, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
verses.2:10: and with every deception of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
verses.2:11: And for this cause God sends them a working of delusion, so that they may believe the lie,
verses.2:12: in order that all may be condemned who did not believe the truth, but delighted in unrighteousness.
verses.2:13: But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation in sanctification by the Spirit and faith in the truth,
verses.2:14: to which He called you through our gospel, for the gaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2:15: So then, brethren, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions which you were taught, whether by word or by our letter.
verses.2:16: Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal consolation and good hope in grace,
verses.2:17: comfort your hearts and strengthen them in every good work and word.
verses.3:1: Finally, pray for us, brethren, that the word of the Lord may speed onward and be glorified, just as it also is among you,
verses.3:2: and that we may be delivered from perverse and evil men; for not all possess faith.
verses.3:3: Yet the Lord is faithful; He shall establish you and guard you from the evil one.
verses.3:4: And we are confident in the Lord regarding you, that what we command, you both do and shall do.
verses.3:5: And may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the endurance of Christ.
verses.3:6: Now we charge you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition which they received from us.
verses.3:7: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we did not act disorderly among you,
verses.3:8: nor did we eat bread from anyone without paying, but in toil and hardship we labored night and day, so that we would not burden any one of you;
verses.3:9: not because we do not have the right, but in order to give ourselves to you as a pattern, so that you should imitate us.
verses.3:10: For indeed when we were with you, we kept charging you with this: "If anyone is unwilling to work, neither let him eat."
verses.3:11: For we hear that some are walking disorderly among you, doing no work at all, yet meddling as busybodies.
verses.3:12: Now we charge and exhort such persons in the Lord Jesus Christ that, working in quietness, they eat their own bread.
verses.3:13: But you, brethren, do not lose heart in doing what is good.
verses.3:14: And if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, mark that person and do not associate with him, so that he may be put to shame.
verses.3:15: And do not consider him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
verses.3:16: Now may the Lord of peace Himself grant you peace continually in every way. The Lord be with you all.
verses.3:17: The greeting is with my own hand—Paul's—which is a sign in every letter; thus I write.
verses.3:18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.

notes.1:8: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads "our Lord Jesus" without "Christ" here and again in 1:12.
notes.1:9: The phrase "from the presence" (apo prosopou) may denote either separation ("away from the presence") or source ("coming from the presence"), echoing Isaiah 2:10, 19, 21.
notes.1:12: The phrase "of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ" shares a single Greek definite article and may also be construed as "of our God and Lord, Jesus Christ."
notes.2:2: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads "the day of the Lord" (kyriou) rather than "the day of Christ."
notes.2:3: The Greek leaves the main clause implied after "for" (supplied here as "that day shall not come"), and reads "the man of lawlessness" (anomias) rather than "the man of sin."
notes.2:6: Paul shifts from the neuter "what restrains" (to katechon) in verse 6 to the masculine "the one who restrains" (ho katechon) in verse 7 without naming the restrainer, variously identified as civil order, an angelic force, or the Holy Spirit.
notes.2:13: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads "from the beginning" (ap' arches) rather than the variant "as firstfruits" (aparchen).
notes.3:3: The Greek tou ponerou can be taken either as masculine ("the evil one") or as neuter ("evil").
notes.3:5: "The love of God" and "the endurance of Christ" may refer to God's love for believers and Christ's own endurance, or to believers' love for God and patient endurance for Christ.
notes.3:6: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads the third-person plural "they received" (parelabosan), rather than the variants "you received" or "he received."
notes.3:11: The Greek uses a play on words between ergazomenous ("working") and periergazomenous ("acting as busybodies").
